course.title: Python — Complete Deep Learning Course
course.description: A genuinely Python-specific, beginner-to-advanced course with concept-first notes, practical coding, dedicated tasks, testing and a complete capstone.
course.curriculumPolicy: Module and lesson counts are determined by the concepts required to learn this language properly; no fixed module/lesson template is imposed.
learningOutcomes: Understand Python from fundamentals to advanced practical programming.

modules.title: Python Foundations
modules.description: Running Python, syntax, indentation and the execution model.

lessons.title: Python Foundations
lessons.description: Running Python, syntax, indentation and the execution model.
learningObjectives: Understand the mental model behind Python Foundations.
Write correct Python code using Python Foundations.
Explain the program flow in your own words.
Handle at least one edge case.
Apply the concept in a practical task.

notes.text: Running Python, syntax, indentation and the execution model.

In this lesson, the student should understand python foundations before trying to memorize syntax. Start with the mental model, then connect each rule to a small program and finally to the practical task.
Python Foundations is important because it appears repeatedly when building real Python programs. A student should be able to explain when to use it, what can go wrong, and how to test the result.

notes.caption: Create a teaching diagram showing the relationship between the main ideas in Python Foundations.

items: Define the main idea behind Python Foundations.
Understand the syntax or API involved.
Trace what happens step by step when the program runs.
Know the common failure cases.
Choose a clear and maintainable implementation.

notes.text: Read the example from top to bottom. Predict the result first. Then run it and compare your prediction with the actual result.

notes.code:
print('Hello, Python!')
name = 'Student'
print(f'Welcome, {name}')

items: Identify the input or starting state.
Identify the important variables/data structures.
Follow each operation in order.
Observe the output or returned value.
Ask what would happen with invalid, empty, very large or unexpected input.
Copying syntax without understanding the data flow.
Ignoring invalid input or boundary cases.
Mixing responsibilities into one large function.
Failing to test the code after changing it.
Using a more complex technique when a simpler one is clearer.
Prefer readable names and small responsibilities.
Validate assumptions at boundaries.
Keep repeated logic reusable.
Test both expected and failure paths.
Use the official language documentation when behavior is uncertain.
I can explain Python Foundations without reading the notes.
I can write a small example from memory.
I can identify at least one edge case.
I can explain one common mistake and how to avoid it.

practicals.title: Guided Practical — Python Foundations
practicals.objective: Use Python Foundations in a small but complete Python exercise.
steps: Change the input and predict the result.
Test an invalid or boundary case.
practicals.starterCode:
print('Hello, Python!')
name = 'Student'
print(f'Welcome, {name}')
practicals.expectedOutput: A working Python program demonstrating Python Foundations.

tasks.title: Dedicated Task — Python Foundations
tasks.description: Build a command-line welcome program that asks for a student's name and prints a formatted introduction.
requirements: The solution must demonstrate Python Foundations.
Use clear naming and structure.

quiz.question: Which statement best describes Python Foundations?
options: It is a core Python programming concept covered in this lesson.

quiz.answer: It is a core Python programming concept covered in this lesson.
